matchstick.title: Balance by numeric difference and single‑stick transformation
matchstick.principle: First compute the decimal values of both sides of the equation (including any operators) to find the numeric imbalance. Then look for a single‑stick move that changes a numeral or operator by exactly that amount, ensuring the resulting equation is numerically correct.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving any matchstick equation, before trying specific stick moves.
matchstick.example: Skipping the numeric imbalance calculation and moving a stick arbitrarily, resulting in an equation that remains false.

matchstick.title: Convert V to X to add 5
matchstick.principle: If the side that must increase contains a V and the numeric imbalance is exactly +5, reposition one of the V’s diagonal sticks so that the V becomes an X, raising that side’s value by 5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the imbalance is +5 and a V appears on the deficient side.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from a V when the imbalance is not +5, which changes the value by the wrong amount.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: Move a vertical I‑stick from a numeral that already has at least one I to another numeral that can accept an extra I without violating Roman‑numeral rules, adjusting the values by ±1.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric imbalance is ±1 and such a transfer is possible.
matchstick.example: Taking an I from a numeral that would become invalid (e.g., leaving a numeral with no I’s) and moving it elsewhere.

matchstick.title: Convert X to V to subtract 5
matchstick.principle: If the side that must decrease contains an X and the numeric imbalance is exactly –5, reposition one of the X’s diagonal sticks so that the X becomes a V, lowering that side’s value by 5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the imbalance is –5 and an X appears on the side that is too large.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from an X when the imbalance is not –5, causing an incorrect numeric change.

matchstick.title: Swap '-' and '=' by moving a horizontal stick
matchstick.principle: If both a minus sign (single horizontal) and an equals sign (two horizontals) are present, you can move one horizontal stick from the equals sign to the minus sign (or vice versa), effectively swapping their meanings while keeping each operator valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric imbalance suggests that a minus should become an equals (or the opposite) and both operators are present.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal from '=' when no '-' exists, leaving an invalid operator.

matchstick.title: Convert '+' to '-' by moving its vertical stick
matchstick.principle: Remove the vertical stick from a plus sign; the remaining horizontal becomes a minus sign, changing the operation from addition to subtraction.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric imbalance indicates that subtraction would fix the equation and a plus sign is present.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical from '+' when a numeral transformation could have resolved the imbalance, leading to an unnecessary operator change.

matchstick.title: Maintain operator validity when moving a stick from '='
matchstick.principle: When relocating a stick from the equality sign, ensure that at least one horizontal stick remains so that the sign stays a valid '=', otherwise it unintentionally becomes a minus sign.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Any time you consider moving a stick from the equals sign.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal from '=' and leaving no horizontals, turning it into an invalid operator.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick across equality when imbalance is 2
matchstick.principle: If the numeric difference between the two sides is exactly 2, move a vertical I‑stick from a numeral on the larger side to a numeral on the smaller side, adjusting each side by 1 and preserving Roman‑numeral validity.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the imbalance is 2 and such a transfer does not create an illegal numeral.
matchstick.example: Moving an I from a side that already lacks I's, creating an invalid numeral, when the imbalance is not exactly 2.

matchstick.title: Prefer numeral adjustments over operator changes
matchstick.principle: When fixing a matchstick equation, first try transformations that change numeral values (e.g., I transfer, V↔X conversion). Only modify operators (e.g., '+' to '-', '-' to '=', etc.) if no numeral move can resolve the numeric imbalance. This avoids unnecessary operator changes that break the equality.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After computing the numeric imbalance, before considering any operator‑changing moves.
matchstick.example: Changing a '+' to '-' when the imbalance could be fixed by converting a V to X, resulting in a numerically incorrect equation.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from a numeral that cannot lose a stick without becoming invalid (e.g., X, V, solitary I)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats any stick as removable without checking whether the source numeral would still be a legal Roman numeral after the removal.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Before moving a stick from a numeral, verify that the remaining sticks still form a valid Roman numeral according to canonical rules.

matchstick.description: Providing an invalid equation after moving a stick (including incomplete or unreachable solutions)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the stick move but neglects to re‑evaluate the arithmetic correctness of the resulting equation.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After any stick relocation, recompute the decimal values of both sides and confirm that the equality holds before finalising the answer.

matchstick.description: Not verifying numeric equality after transformation; resulting equation may be syntactically valid but numerically false
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes that a syntactically correct Roman‑numeral expression is automatically correct, skipping the final arithmetic check.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always perform a numeric check after the transformation; if the equality fails, backtrack and try a different stick move.

matchstick.description: Moving more than one stick (or removing multiple sticks) violates the single‑stick rule
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes interprets a transformation as requiring two separate moves (e.g., turning '+' into '-' and simultaneously adding a stick elsewhere).
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Count the sticks being moved: exactly one stick must be removed from its original location and placed elsewhere; no extra sticks may be added or removed.

matchstick.description: Creating a non‑canonical Roman numeral (e.g., duplicate V, duplicate L, duplicate D, or more than three I's in a row)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on stick placement without enforcing the standard Roman‑numeral formation rules.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each move, verify that every numeral conforms to canonical Roman‑numeral syntax before accepting the solution.
